item.title: Shocking New Louvre Heist Footage Released to the Public
item.description: The video shows how the thieves made it in and out of the museum's Apollo Gallery almost seamlessly with the nation's crown jewels.

item.title: How to Piss Off Trump
item.description: A mysterious public artwork on the National Mall, the Philadelphia Art Museum's ongoing rebrand debacle, new Louvre heist footage, and Yoko Ono's relentless positivity.

item.title: New York Academy of Art Presents “Chubb Fellows & Friends”
item.description: Featuring past fellows alongside a broader circle of artists linked to the Academy, the show brings together work by Danica Lundy, Dana Schutz, Tschabalala Self, Amy Sherald, and more.

item.title: Edward Zutrau Was a Chromatic Rebel
item.description: He combined the reductive strain of Abstract Expressionism with the principles and style of Japanese ink painting, for something uniquely his own.

item.title: Fra Angelico Etched the Divine in Stone
item.description: The veiled symbolism of the artist's marble and stones has largely flown under the radar, but these mystical depths are too profound to miss out on.

item.title: Art Problems: How Do I Get Into the Whitney Biennial?
item.description: Conventional wisdom says there isn’t much you can do, but Paddy Johnson knows that’s not the whole story.

item.title: Falling in Love With Vintage Gay Films
item.description: What it’s like to “rediscover” vintage gay adult films from the 1970s and 1980s in a moment of state repression.

item.title: Remembering Harvey Pratt, Roger Allers, and Robert Burleigh
item.description: This week, we honor the designer of the Native American Veterans Memorial, a Disney animator, a picture book illustrator, and others.

item.title: Queens Museum Leader Sally Tallant to Step Down After Seven Years
item.description: Under Tallant, the museum secured a $26 million expansion allocation from the city, but also drew controversy and criticism.

item.title: Gabrielle Goliath to Seek Legal Action After Axed Venice Biennale Pavilion
item.description: The artist reportedly alleges that South Africa’s minister of culture acted unconstitutionally in canceling her commission, which included references to Gaza.
